title: Reward and Punishment
lead: The belief that God rewards faithfulness and punishes wrongdoing, and the debate over how and when he does it. Chronicles is famous for showing the results within a single lifetime, while Job, Ecclesiastes and some psalms protest that life often looks otherwise.

sections.h: Reward and punishment in the Bible
sections.b: The covenant in Deuteronomy sets blessing and curse before Israel: obedience brings life in the land, and unfaithfulness brings defeat and exile (Deuteronomy 28; Deuteronomy 30:15–20). Kings judges each king by this standard, though the punishment often falls on a later generation, as the exile falls for Manasseh's sins (2 Kings 23:26–27). Ezekiel insists that each person bears his own guilt (Ezekiel 18). Chronicles goes furthest: in its retelling, faithful kings prosper and unfaithful ones suffer in their own day, often with a prophet sent to explain why. Job, Ecclesiastes and Psalm 73 wrestle with the times when the wicked prosper and the righteous suffer, and Jesus rejects the idea that every disaster is a punishment for its victims' sins (Luke 13:1–5; John 9:1–3).
